1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module eighteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. This module covers pacing, method and final review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. A time plan for sixty items in one hundred twenty minutes. A method to read an item, spot the binding concern and eliminate distractors. How to handle multiple-response items. Policies and logistics on exam day. A final review checklist and a plan for the last week.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedarbrook Outfitters
1.text: Our running case is Cedarbrook Outfitters. Cedarbrook Outfitters. The team meets the topic of this module. Your job: decide, step by step, which choice fits best.

1.title: Time Plan
1.text: Time Plan. The figure shows this: Time plan for sixty items in one hundred twenty minutes: a first pass of about eighty minutes, thirty minutes for marked items, ten minutes for final checks. sixty items in one hundred twenty minutes is two minutes per item, which is generous: you can read carefully. First pass (about eighty minutes): answer what you know in about eighty seconds, mark the rest and move on. Second pass (about thirty minutes): work the marked items with a fresh mind.

1.title: Time Plan, continued
1.text: Time Plan, continued. Last ten minutes: check that multiple-response items have the right number of answers and that nothing is blank. Never leave an item blank; make your best choice. Do not spend more than about three minutes on one item at the first pass. There is no domain pass mark; only the total scaled score (seven hundred twenty) counts. Exam tip: Calm and steady beats fast. With two minutes per item, the usual errors come from misreading the question, not from running out of time.

1.title: Reading an Item
1.text: Reading an Item. Read the last sentence first ("What is the most appropriate action?") and note how many answers to select. Read the scenario for the binding concern: accuracy, data sensitivity, cost or speed, context length, who is accountable, which feature fits. Predict the answer before you read the options. Compare the options with your prediction and the ten decision rules (Module zero).

1.title: Reading an Item, continued
1.text: Reading an Item, continued. "confident", "cites a section", "before sending". Verify against the authoritative source. "vague", "generic", "too long". Improve the prompt (context, format, constraints). "large project", "multiple parts". Decompose into reviewed steps. "current", "today's price". Web search. "comprehensive", "multi-source", "report with citations". Research. "complex reasoning", "logic error". Extended thinking (with verification). "high volume", "fast", "low cost". Lighter model, lower effort. "same background every time". Project. "repeatable procedure". Skill. "latest Drive files", "email". Connector (within permissions, approvals). "customer names", "account numbers", "health", "policy restricts". Remove or anonymize; approved tool; policy.

1.title: Reading an Item, continued
1.text: Reading an Item, continued. "hiring", "credit", "benefits", "legal advice". Qualified human decides; disclose. "drifted", "very long chat". Summarize and restart. "not working". Diagnose and change one thing. "A P I (application programming interface)", "integrate", "automate with code". Escalate. Exam tip: The cause or the constraint is usually in the stem. Use it before looking at the options.

1.title: Eliminating Distractors
1.text: Eliminating Distractors. Cross out options that. Trust without verifying ("send it because it sounds sure"). Use self-assessment as validation ("ask Claude if it is sure"). Go to an extreme ("always", "never", "only") without reason. Skip the human where stakes are high. Share sensitive data against policy, or rely on "don't retain" as protection. Over-tool (Research for a one-line fact) or under-tool (chat for a multi-source report). Redo everything when one change would do. Improvise technical integration instead of escalating. Hide or fake (A I use, reviews, sources). Then pick the option that verifies, protects data, fits the task and keeps a person accountable. Exam tip: Change an answer only when you can name the rule it breaks.

1.title: Multiple-response items
1.text: Multiple-response items. The stem says exactly how many to choose ("Select two"). Choose that number. Judge each option on its own: is it true and does it answer the question? Do not assume the two answers are related; sometimes they are separate good practices. If you are stuck, eliminate the clearly wrong options first.

1.title: Policies and Logistics
1.text: Policies and Logistics. Registration. Through the Anthropic Partner Academy and Pearson V U E; online proctored or test center. Reschedule or cancel. Up to twenty-four hours before; later changes forfeit the fee. I D. Valid, unexpired government photo I D; the name must match the registration exactly. Accommodations. Request and get approval from Pearson V U E before scheduling. Agreements. You accept a confidentiality and non-disclosure agreement; never share exam content. Conduct. Stay in view of the webcam if online; clear desk; no phones, watches, headphones or notes; no communication. Retakes. fourteen or thirty or ninety days; max four attempts per rolling twelve months; fee per attempt.

1.title: Policies and Logistics, continued
1.text: Policies and Logistics, continued. Result. Pass or fail and scaled score, plus percent correct per domain. Validity and renewal. twelve months; on-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment; a lapsed credential needs the full exam again. Appeals. Within fourteen days through Pearson V U E support; scoring standard and individual items are not appealable. The guide is version one point zero (July two thousand twenty-six). Check the Partner Academy for the current guide, fee and rules before you book.

1.title: Final Review Checklist
1.text: Final Review Checklist. [ ] I can state the ten decision rules without looking. [ ] I can build a strong prompt and decompose a complex request. [ ] I know the error types (hallucination, wrong numbers, outdated, overstated abilities, bias) and the checks that catch them. [ ] I know when a qualified human must review. [ ] I can choose between web search, thinking and Research, and between Haiku, Sonnet and Opus style models. [ ] I can decide to restart, summarize or persist. [ ] I can configure a Project (instructions and knowledge), and I know connectors, Skills and memory. [ ] I can classify data sensitivity and name the safe action.

1.title: Final Review Checklist, continued
1.text: Final Review Checklist, continued. [ ] I know the main points of A I policy, governance and ethics. [ ] I can diagnose a weak output and optimize a workflow. [ ] I know what to escalate and how to brief a Developer. [ ] I have used Claude to build a Project and evaluated its outputs for accuracy and bias.

1.title: The last week
1.text: The last week. Seven to four days before: reread the notes of the heaviest domains (Output Evaluation, then Workflow and Solution Design, then Governance and Prompting), redo their scenario questions, and write down every miss with the reason. Three days before: walk through the decision chooser in Module seventeen aloud; reread the names and values table. The day before: light review only: the ten decision rules and the time plan. Check your I D, registration name and test setup, and sleep. On the day: arrive or log in early, read each item's last sentence first, and keep to the time plan.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Time: two minutes per item; first pass about eighty minutes; mark and return. Method: Last sentence first, binding concern, predict, eliminate. Pick: Verified, data-safe, fit to task, person accountable. Multiple response: Choose exactly the stated number. I D: Name must match registration exactly. Cancel: At least twenty-four hours before. Retake: fourteen or thirty or ninety days; max four per rolling twelve months. Pass: seven hundred twenty scaled of one hundred to one thousand; total score only. Valid: twelve months; free on-time renewal assessment. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
